result:
Created two self-contained JUnit 5 test classes (Java 8 compatible, no lambdas/diamonds), both compile and pass:

- `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DurationUtilsAgentTest.java` — 24 tests covering `accept` (null consumer/duration, value propagation, exception propagation), `get`/`getMillis`/`getSeconds` (default fallback, empty key), `getNanosOfMilli`/deprecated `getNanosOfMiili` (including null duration), `isPositive`, `of(Runnable/Consumer)` (value + exception propagation), `since`, `toChronoUnit` (all enum values + null), `toDuration`, `toMillisInt` (including `Integer.MAX_VALUE`/`MIN_VALUE` clamping and null), `zeroIfNull`, and the deprecated public constructor.
- `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/StopWatchAgentTest.java` — 45 tests covering state transitions (`start`/`stop`/`suspend`/`resume`/`reset`) and their illegal-state errors, split/unsplit behavior (including that repeated `split()` while running just accumulates splits, and `getSplits()` being unmodifiable), timing accessors (`getTime`, `getNanoTime`, `getDuration`, `getSplitDuration`, deprecated `getSplitTime`/`getStartTime`/`getStopTime`), formatting (`formatTime`, `formatSplitTime`, `toString`, `toSplitString` with/without message), and the `run`/`get`/`runT`/`getT` delegation methods including checked-exception propagation.
